sections.h2: How do you file a deed with the Hillsdale County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Walk in to Room 212 of the County Office Building, 33 McCollum St., Hillsdale 49242, or phone (517) 437-2231. The window is staffed Monday to Friday from 8:30 in the morning until 5:00 in the afternoon. E-filings can be transmitted at any hour, but clerks work them only during posted hours and not on holidays.

Four e-recording vendors are approved: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. They are paid by ACH, may add charges of their own, and return the recorded document electronically. Any e-filing that violates the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected.

A personal check will not pay for a paper filing, though certified funds are fine (cashier's checks and money orders). Staff do not draft documents, supply templates, or say anything that could be read as legal advice.

sections.h2: What does Hillsdale County charge for recording?
sections.html:
Recording a document costs a flat $30.00 under MCL 600.2567, as amended by PA 224 of 2016, with side charges listed below.

Statutory deed fees posted by Hillsdale County, effective October 1, 2016
Charge forPrice
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 total
Each extra instrument released$3.00
Treasurer's tax certificate (five descriptions)$5.00
Name search$5.00 floor, then 50 cents per year
Page of a real estate record$1.00
Certifying a copy$5.00

Lien searches at the state or federal level cost $3.00 per name, and plats copy at $2.00 per page. A transfer tax calculator is posted on the register's page for planning, with the final amount settled when the deed is presented.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Hillsdale County sale?
sections.html:
Start by counting $500 blocks in the price, rounding up, and multiply the count by $4.30. The number is 55 cents for the county, from MCL 207.504, plus $3.75 for the state, from MCL 207.525.

Take a $175,000 sale: 350 blocks, $1,312.50 for the state, $192.50 for the county, $1,505.00 in all. A house at the county median of $176,100 rounds to $176,500, making 353 blocks and $1,517.90.

  • The deed shows the price, or an affidavit does.
  • A claimed exemption is stated on the instrument.
  • Statutory exemptions: MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state).
  • A land contract is exempt while title stays with the seller, and the deed that completes it must reference the contract.

sections.h2: Which 2018 law changes still matter for a Hillsdale County deed?
sections.html:
A notice dated June 22, 2018 went from the register to title companies, attorneys and lenders about Public Acts 191 to 200, signed two days before. Most of the changes started on September 19, 2018.

  • A deed from a surviving owner must be backed by a certified death certificate recorded earlier, cited by liber and page, or filed alongside as a separate recording. Attaching a copy no longer meets MCL 565.48.
  • Documents signed outside Michigan follow Michigan's recording rules too, except for page layout (MCL 565.203).
  • Anything partly in a foreign language comes with an English translation (MCL 565.201).

Court orders need the clerk's certification and seal, an acknowledgment cannot omit its date, and fees are collected when a document is handed over.

sections.h2: What does the Hillsdale register check on every deed?
sections.html:
A checklist from the register spells out what a deed must contain, and a deed lacking one item can be bounced.

  • Ink signatures, each with a printed name that agrees with the notary's wording (MCL 565.201).
  • A mailing address for the grantee, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledging any deed signed in the state.
  • Readable black type of 10 points or more on white 20 pound sheets, leaving 2.5 inches blank at the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere, under a line naming what the paper records.
  • Property value stated on the deed or in an attached affidavit.
  • Social Security numbers cut back to four digits.
  • Trust certificates that meet MCL 565.432 and 565.433.

Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 also had to say whether any male grantors were married or single, a rule that no longer reaches newer deeds.

sections.h2: How do you search Hillsdale County deed records?
sections.html:
The register's page offers search by full text, using optical character recognition, and by name, date, and liber and page. Tract books are linked through Kofile. An owner who wants a deed corrected should know that the office cannot change or alter a document already recorded or in the middle of recording.

Title companies do much of the research for a sale. The register's page names three in the city of Hillsdale: Public Title, Midstate Title and Bell Title Tri County. Ask whichever one handles your closing to confirm the transfer tax figure, since the register collects it with the recording fee.

sections.h2: What does the Hillsdale County Treasurer require before and after a closing?
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 calls for a certificate from the Treasurer on any warranty deed, land contract, or land contract assignment carrying a warranty clause. Five descriptions cost $5.00, and the office answers at (517) 437-4700.

A yearly delinquent tax notice from the Treasurer describes the closing stage of Michigan's foreclosure process. One cutoff date decides whose name is printed in a two week newspaper ad before the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. A little later the office refuses partial payments and personal or business checks, taking only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards (3% convenience fee). The notice presses owners to pay before a valuable property is lost.

Anyone with an old balance should ask for a payoff before listing the house, because the deed cannot move until the certificate issues.

Territorial lawmakers described the county in 1829 and it was organized in 1835. Its name refers to rolling terrain. The city of Hillsdale is both seat and largest city, and Hillsdale College is based there. At 607 square miles, the county is the only one in Michigan bordering both Indiana and Ohio, and it holds Michigan's southernmost point. Two separate St. Joseph Rivers begin here, one flowing toward Lake Michigan and one toward the Maumee. McCourtie Park and Slayton Arboretum are local parks. Jackson, Calhoun, Lenawee and Branch counties border it in Michigan, with Fulton and Williams counties in Ohio and Steuben County in Indiana to the south.

Winter highs in January average 29 degrees and July highs 82, and June brings the most rain, about 4.3 inches.

Headcount is flat. The 2025 estimate is 45,738, against 45,746 in 2020 and 46,688 in 2010. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show 17,860 households, a $176,100 median home value, 82.0% of homes owner-occupied, $64,242 median household income, $832 median rent and 23.2% of residents aged 65 or more. Owners live in more than four of five homes, so a typical recording here is a home sale.

A free Property Alert service from the register warns landowners of possible property fraud.

faqs.q: What does a Hillsdale County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: $30.00 buys the filing of a whole document. Transfer tax comes on top for a sale, and a warranty deed also needs a $5.00 certificate from the County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Hillsdale County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile or CSC/Ingeo. Payment goes by ACH, and the vendors may add fees of their own.

faqs.q: Is a personal check good for a Hillsdale County filing?
faqs.a: No. The office takes certified funds, such as a cashier's check or a money order, in its place.

faqs.q: When is the Hillsdale County register open?
faqs.a: Weekdays, from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., in Room 212 at 33 McCollum St. Electronic filings may be transmitted at any hour but are handled only during those hours.

faqs.q: What would a $175,000 Hillsdale County sale owe in transfer tax?
faqs.a: $1,505.00. That is 350 blocks of $500 at $4.30 each, split into $1,312.50 for the state and $192.50 for the county.
